events.title: Sarnath
events.summary: Sarnath connects Śākyamuni, the first-turning-of-the-Dharma tradition, early monastic memory and later Buddhist pilgrimage to a real archaeological place.
events.displayDate: Early Buddhist tradition through the site's development to the 12th century CE

events.title: Longmen dedicatory inscription record (object placeholder)
events.summary: A dedicatory inscription can connect image, donor, vow, date and cave location as a traceable object.
events.displayDate: Object pending; late Northern Wei through Tang

events.title: Longmen Grottoes
events.summary: Longmen brings Luoyang, imperial patronage, Buddhist images and inscriptions into one material landscape.
events.displayDate: Late Northern Wei through Tang focus

events.title: Jizang
events.summary: Jizang's teaching and commentary provide a case for Buddhist thought, textual interpretation and urban networks across the Sui–Tang transition.

events.title: Kong Yingda
events.summary: Kong Yingda represents how Tang classical learning entered state education, commentary and institutional knowledge production.

events.title: Chang'an
events.summary: Chang'an compressed court, state education, monasteries, Daoist institutions, markets and international travellers into one city.

events.title: Chang'an Daoist monastic network
events.summary: Daoist activity in Chang'an relied on multiple institutions, ritual services, ordination records and court connections rather than one building.

events.title: Chang'an–Luoyang imperial corridor
events.summary: The route organizes political, educational, religious and human movement between the two capitals as a spatial research frame.

events.title: Classical commentary
events.summary: Commentary organizes classics, inherited interpretation, textual criticism and teaching into transmissible knowledge structures.

events.title: Daoist institutional inscription rubbing (object placeholder)
events.summary: Inscriptions and rubbings can anchor institutions, figures, dates and patronage in verifiable textual objects.

events.title: Dunhuang
events.summary: Dunhuang connects Buddhist art, textual preservation, travel routes and multilingual culture.

events.title: Guozijian
events.summary: The Guozijian connects the Five Classics, commentary, examination and state education within a traceable institutional line.

events.title: Kucha
events.summary: Kucha keeps a pilgrimage route from becoming a straight line from Chang'an to India; it was a region where languages, religions and media intersected.
events.displayDate: Sui–Tang transport and Buddhist exchange context

events.title: Louguan Daoist institution
events.summary: As an institutional record, Louguan helps separate Laozi legend, Daoist figures, monastic space and later sacred-site narratives.
events.displayDate: Sui–Tang and later narratives; Guanzhong focus

events.title: Luoyang
events.summary: Luoyang connects imperial politics, transport networks, Buddhist transmission and classical culture as a counterpoint to Chang'an.

events.title: Mount Wutai
events.summary: Mount Wutai combines a real mountain landscape, monastic networks and Buddhist sacred narratives, making the museum's two-layer geography visible.
events.displayDate: Sui–Tang Buddhist geography and later sacred narratives

events.title: Official-learning ritual object record (object placeholder)
events.summary: A ritual object can connect the concept of li with school space, participants and concrete action.
events.displayDate: Object pending; Sui–Tang educational ritual context

events.title: Pilgrimage and transmission
events.summary: Pilgrimage became durable knowledge transmission through translation, cataloguing, teaching and institutional collaboration.

events.title: Sui–Tang Daoist institutional records
events.summary: This research-layer text collection helps distinguish Daoist biographies, institutional history and later genealogical narratives.
events.displayDate: Scope of Sui–Tang Daoist institutional research

events.title: The founding and unification of the Sui
events.summary: The founding and unification of the Sui provides political context for Sui–Tang institutions, capitals and networks of knowledge.

events.title: Yan Shigu
events.summary: Yan Shigu connects early Tang textual editing and commentary with state knowledge projects.

events.title: Zhongnan Mountains
events.summary: The Zhongnan Mountains are a real landscape near Chang'an and a layered setting for cultivation, reclusion and religious narrative.

events.title: Li Shimin
events.summary: Li Shimin's courtly, educational and religious institutional context helps explain why Chang'an became a meeting point for different networks of knowledge and belief.

events.title: Cheng Xuanying
events.summary: Cheng Xuanying offers an entry into early Tang interpretation of the Daodejing and Zhuangzi and its Daoist knowledge networks.

events.title: Classical commentary manuscript record (object placeholder)
events.summary: The object card connects the Corrected Meanings and Guozijian to manuscripts, folios and practices of reading.
events.displayDate: Object record pending; Tang classical-learning context

events.title: Corrected Meanings of the Five Classics
events.summary: The Corrected Meanings provides an entry into how Tang classical commentary entered state education and regimes of interpretation.

events.title: Daodejing commentary manuscript record (object placeholder)
events.summary: The object record reserves an archive entry for manuscript form, writing layers and provenance of Tang Daodejing commentaries.

events.title: Form and emptiness
events.summary: Form and emptiness is one of the Heart Sutra's most cited expressions, but it must be read within a specific version, passage structure and Prajnaparamita context.

events.title: Form is not different from emptiness
events.summary: This line circulated widely in Chinese Buddhism, but it must be read within its paragraph and textual version.
events.displayDate: Sui–Tang Chinese translation and circulation context

events.title: Heart Sutra
events.summary: The Heart Sutra presents Prajñāpāramitā thought in a highly condensed form and became one of the most widely circulated texts in Chinese Buddhism.
events.displayDate: Chinese translation and circulation: Sui–Tang focus

events.title: Heart Sutra manuscript leaf (object placeholder)
events.summary: The object card places a Heart Sutra passage within paper, ink, writing, preservation and circulation, but is not yet tied to a specific collection.
events.displayDate: Object record pending; Sui–Tang circulation context

events.title: Inscription record for a translation institution (object placeholder)
events.summary: The object card separates translation institutions from biography and looks for material carriers in buildings, inscriptions and institutional memory.
events.displayDate: Object record pending; Tang translation-institution context

events.title: Nalanda
events.summary: Nalanda places the pilgrimages of Xuanzang and Yijing within a concrete institution and transregional network rather than an abstract India.
events.displayDate: Sui–Tang pilgrimage and transregional knowledge networks

events.title: No wisdom and no attainment
events.summary: The line invites a distinction between the sutra's context of non-attainment and a modern denial of knowledge.
events.displayDate: Heart Sutra Chinese translation and circulation context

events.title: Received Chinese version of the Heart Sutra
events.summary: A version placeholder for the first passage display; the precise edition remains under review.

events.title: Record of the Western Regions of the Great Tang
events.summary: The Record turns a pilgrim's travel experience into an account of geography, institutions, cities and religious sites.

events.title: Seeing the five aggregates as empty
events.summary: The line compresses seeing, the five aggregates and emptiness into a short phrase that must be read in a specific version and context.
events.displayDate: Heart Sutra Chinese translation and circulation context

events.title: State-school classics scroll (object placeholder)
events.summary: A scroll object can show how classics entered official learning through copying, collation and teaching.

events.title: These dharmas have the characteristic of emptiness
events.summary: The line places emptiness within a description of dharmas and helps demonstrate the relation among concept, passage and version layers.
events.displayDate: Heart Sutra Chinese translation and circulation context

events.title: Translation catalogue manuscript (object placeholder)
events.summary: Catalogue objects can record translated titles, versions, attribution and institutional organization of textual circulation.

events.title: Xuanzang
events.summary: Xuanzang connects a pilgrimage for learning with translation and institutional life in Chang'an.

events.title: Chang'an translation-bureau network
events.summary: Translation was collaborative work supported by monastic space, language roles, textual checking and imperial patronage.

events.title: Foundation of the Tang dynasty
events.summary: The dynastic transition of 618 reorganized the political, educational and religious resource environment of Chang'an.

events.title: Hongwen Institute
events.summary: The Hongwen Institute offers an institutional entry into Tang court collections, scholarly consultation and education.

events.title: Wu Zhao (Wu Zetian)
events.summary: Wu Zhao's political practice and religious patronage make the institutions, rituals and later memories of Chang'an and Luoyang available for comparison.

events.title: Xuanzang departs Chang'an
events.summary: Around 629, Xuanzang's journey connected Chang'an with pilgrimage networks across the Hexi Corridor, Central Asia and South Asia.

events.title: Xuanzang's western pilgrimage route
events.summary: The route places Chang'an, the Hexi Corridor, Central Asia and South Asia in one research view without treating every node as a verified day-by-day itinerary.

events.title: Compilation project of the Corrected Meanings of the Five Classics
events.summary: A multi-year early Tang editorial project brought commentarial traditions into state education and examination knowledge.

events.title: Yijing
events.summary: Yijing connects maritime pilgrimage, learning in South Asia and the production of Chinese Buddhist translations.

events.title: Xuanzang returns to Chang'an
events.summary: After Xuanzang returned to Chang'an, pilgrimage experience became long-term work in translation, teaching and monastic institutions.

events.title: Sima Chengzhen
events.summary: Sima Chengzhen connects mountain cultivation, Daoist lineages and Tang imperial patronage.

events.title: Establishment of the Great Ci'en Monastery
events.summary: The monastery created a new institutional setting for Buddhism, translation and imperial patronage in Chang'an.

events.title: Great Ci'en Monastery
events.summary: Great Ci'en Monastery is a core institutional entry for connecting Xuanzang, translation, monastic networks and Chang'an's urban space.

events.title: First construction of the Great Wild Goose Pagoda
events.summary: The initial phase around 652 linked the preservation of texts and images with translation and visible urban architecture.

events.title: Great Wild Goose Pagoda site
events.summary: The site connects Xuanzang, translation, textual preservation and the urban space of Chang'an.
events.displayDate: Founded in the Tang; phases pending

events.title: Yijing departs by sea
events.summary: Around 671, Yijing travelled south by sea, showing that pilgrimage and transmission were not limited to an overland route west of Chang'an.

events.title: Establishment of the Wu Zhou
events.summary: The political transition of 690 changed imperial representation, the two-capital system and the allocation of religious resources.

events.title: Yijing returns to Tang territory
events.summary: Around 695, Yijing's return brought maritime travel experience into translation, writing and institutional networks.

events.title: Institutional expansion in the Kaiyuan era
events.summary: The Kaiyuan era provides a range for studying expansion in court, education, religious institutions and transregional exchange.

events.title: An Lushan Rebellion begins
events.summary: War beginning in 755 disrupted the two capitals and changed the demographic, fiscal and institutional environment of religious life.

events.title: End of the An Lushan Rebellion
events.summary: The end of warfare around 763 did not restore the pre-war order but opened a long restructuring of finance, regional power and institutions.

events.title: Huichang religious policies
events.summary: Policies around 845 sharply changed the property, personnel and public standing of Buddhist and other religious institutions.

events.title: The Tang-end political transition
events.summary: The political transition around 907 marks the exhibition's Sui–Tang boundary while reminding us that institutions and textual networks do not disappear in one year.
